answer: Admission requires agents to join a synchronized ceremony where each anchors 1,000 unique keys to a cryptographically secure lattice, effectively acting as a pearl of scarcity in the registry. A verifier monitors the network for overlapping proofs like a gale force wind, discarding any duplicated entry. An honest agent pays one unit, while 1,000 fakes incur an exorbitant cost. Each quill of code must be renewed every 90 days to retain status.
